requirements.requirement: Cron job on node1 runs /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15
requirements.summary: Root crontab entry '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' was installed and verified present both before and after the mandated restart, confirming persistence.
Log file exists, receives appended output on manual invocation both pre- and post-restart, and retained its prior content across the reboot, demonstrating durable append behavior.

requirements.requirement: The maintenance script must actually be runnable (necessary precondition discovered broken during execution)
requirements.summary: Executor found the script corrupted (contained leftover heredoc terminator and setup commands) and non-executable, contradicting the prepare baseline hash; rewrote it to valid #!/bin/sh content, set 0755, and confirmed clean execution and persistence after reboot.

requirements.requirement: crond service must be running and enabled at boot so the schedule actually fires
requirements.summary: crond was found stopped; executor added it to the default runlevel and started it, then confirmed it auto-started and remained enabled after the reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with full pre/disruption/post transition
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id fd36f101-..., crond started, cron entry, log content, script perms) was captured; a native reboot was issued with an acknowledgement returned before disconnection; repeated polling through connection failures observed the bounded disruption; a new boot_id (bbc434bb-...) confirmed the actual restart, matching the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot; post-restart checks directly confirmed crond auto-started/enabled, the cron entry persisted, the script remained intact/executable, the log retained pre-restart data, and a fresh manual run appended successfully.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied: the cron entry for /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance at 02:15 with log redirection is installed and confirmed durable across a reboot, crond is enabled and running, the previously corrupted/non-executable script was repaired and verified, and the log correctly retains appended output. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also executed to a high standard on node1, showing a healthy pre-restart baseline, a genuine boot-identity change, and full post-restart recovery of the cron configuration, script, and log data. Minor hygiene notes (a reverted diagnostic log line and an uncleaned /tmp/reboot.log) are low-risk and do not affect task functionality.
limitations: No direct observation of the cron job firing at its scheduled 02:15 time exists in the captured evidence; satisfaction of the schedule relies on verified crontab content, script correctness, and crond state rather than an actual 02:15 trigger.

The prepare-time baseline script hash does not match the corrupted content observed by the executor, so it cannot be fully determined from this evidence alone whether the corruption was pre-existing at prepare time or introduced between prepare and executor stages; this is treated as pre-existing state per the executor's uncontradicted account.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command timeline is mostly directly purposeful: cron installation, permission/service fixes, script repair, and the mandated restart evidence collection all map clearly to task outcomes. Two minor items are notable: (1) cmd-cd6e0acbff4647db ran the still-corrupted script manually before the corruption was discovered, appending a spurious error line ('SCRIPT: not found') to the log; this was a reasonable diagnostic step (it is what surfaced the corruption) and was fully reverted via the truncate in cmd-8638f12a99964ed0, so it is bounded and low-risk. (2) The reboot command redirected output to /tmp/reboot.log, which was not cleaned up afterward and is visible as new residue in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; this is a small, low-risk leftover tied directly to the mandated restart step, not an unrelated mutation. No failed/conflicting services, no unsafe exposure, and no package-state damage were observed; the listening-sockets and temp-file diffs across the reboot are otherwise expected artifacts of the restart itself.
